1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.

2. Model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 10–15 days of the forecast, then gradually corrects — apply a downward adjustment of 3–8% for days 10–20 if the prior 5–10 days show rising prices.

3. After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — dampen forecast by 5–10% for the 3–5 days following a spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.

4. Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — increase forecast by 2–5% for the last 5–7 days if the prior 10 days show downward trend or mean reversion.

5. Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–20 day window — if the 30-day history shows a clear peak followed by decline, reduce forecast by 3–7% for the 10–20 day forecast window.

6. Model overreacts to recent volatility — if the last 5 days show high volatility or sharp moves, reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.

7. Model tends to underestimate prices when the 30-day history is trending downward — if the last 10 days are below 75% of the 30-day average, increase forecast by 3–7% for the next 5–10 days.
